## Notes

**Quick read:** Mom of six filming a blond toddler boy (about a year old) on her hip at home; confident, fast yapper who ships volume (11 videos, 8 approved, all 8 ran as ads) but ROAS is weak at 0.67.
**Best next move:** get the two Sep 8 revisions (hands off baby) re-shot and back in, then push her off the "Velcro baby, holds 50 lbs, prints are stunning" script toward a new hook, since that script has run 8 times and is not converting.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- On camera: young mom of six ("As a mom of six"), always the same blond toddler boy (roughly 12 to 15 months, legs dangling, sits on her hip). Filmed at home in bright open living rooms and kitchens; three different backdrops (grey wood-floor living room, teal kitchen with tile, and an evening room with a lantern ceiling light). Casual outfits (white tee, teal tank, green set, cream sweater), no makeup vibe, very real.
- Format: pure yapper, talking straight to camera, handheld or propped. Bubbly, quick, lots of pointing and hand talking. Typical length 19 to 48 seconds. Always demos the hardware: points at the front buckle, shows the strap adjuster, explains the safety loop ("this little piece... if the buckle comes undone baby is still secure"), and does a slow turn to show the back buckle.
- Hooks she opens with: "If you have a Velcro baby, you need to check the Bambora Sling Carriers out", "Velcro Babies! Velcro Baby Mamas!", "As a mom of six, this Bambora Sling Carrier is my absolute favorite", "A very affordable sling carrier is this Bambora Sling Carrier", "The carrier that you need in your life". Recurring beats: holds up to 50 pounds, "the prints are stunning / so stinking cute", fall pumpkin patches and zoo trips, weight off back and shoulders.
- What worked: 8 approved, every one run as ads (the Aug 17 and Aug 20 pairs ran in 2 ads each). But $370 spend for $247 GMV (3 purchases), ROAS 0.67, $25 earned. Volume is great, conversion is not.
- Rejected: Jul 28 (e4e9286a), her first one, a product-only "POV: you finally get the sling carrier that all the moms are talking about" unboxing with burned-in text and no baby wearing; script also said "still have all my mobility". No review comment recorded.
- Revision requested Sep 8, both still open: 77f64db2 (both arms out wide around 34s, and she says "look, hands-free") and 3dd012ea (both hands off around 34s and 42s). Both reviews were warm and asked for a re-take of just those segments.
- Safety and checklist: seat is under his bottom in every sheet and the safety loop is in use and explained. Her one habit is letting go: she talks with both hands and does the turn-around with an arm flung out. In approved sheets too there are moments where the supporting hand is not visible (for example 7a0e4515 at 5s and 61a39bda at 9s, mid-turn with an arm out; e1aef166 at 7s and 32s). The Sep 8 "hands-free" line is a retired claim. Toddler legs often hang straight down, fine for his size since the seat is under him.
- Strengths: natural on camera, clear hardware demo (the safety loop explanation is exactly right), relatable big-family authority, reliable output.
- To improve: keep one hand on him during the turn-around; drop "hands-free"; find a fresh opener, because the Velcro baby plus 50 lbs plus stunning prints script is saturated. Try wrist and arm relief with six kids, or an outdoor pumpkin patch shot instead of the living room.
